newsitem.title: USA: Indianapolis Mayor unveils arena financing plans.
newsitem.headline: Indianapolis Mayor unveils arena financing plans.

text.p: Indianapolis Mayor Stephen Goldsmith unveiled a public-private partly bond-financed plan for a new $175 million downtown arena for the Indiana Pacers basketball team.
At least $104 million of the arena financing will come from private sources and the rest from public revenue streams, Goldsmith said Wednesday.
Pacers owners Herb and Melvin Simon have contributed $2 million toward the arena thus far and will include another $55 million from ticket tax and parking revenues, Goldsmith said.
Another 16 investors in the Circle Centre Mall downtown have committed $3.7 million annually for debt service on $37 million of bonds for the arena, Goldsmith said.
Eli Lilly and Co has pledged the use of land adjacent to the arena site valued at $10 million for parking and construction staging as well, Goldsmith said.
On the public side, state income and sales taxes derived from a new professional sports development district will be used to back $50 million of bonds, Goldsmith said.
State lawmakers and the city-county council recently approved creation of the district, for which state revenues will be capped at $5 million, the mayor added.

Remaining financing includes a $4.7 million infrastructure grant, $9.3 million of restricted reserves from the Capital Improvement Board and $7 million in revenues from the Circle Centre Mall designated for downtown development.
The city-county council is expected to vote on the final financing plans for the arena on Monday.
The arena project is scheduled to be completed by fall 1999 and will include approximately 65 luxury suites and 2,000 club seats.
